title: Season 1, Ep 2: Pick your base
oneliner: After a solution-architect certification gives you the infrastructure, platform, and application base, your starting point - developer, operations, or other - shapes your path into the architect role.
says: Continuing the season: the certification from Episode 1 gives detailed knowledge of the infrastructure, platform, and application layers - the three critical layers for a solution architect. With that base in place, your next step depends on your current experience: some of you are developers, some from operations, and the path differs by background.
explained: The episode's real message is that the AI architect role is a convergence point, not an entry-level job. Developers bring system-building instincts, operations people bring reliability instincts, platform people bring standardization instincts. The certification exists to fill the shared base - the three layers - so that each background can build from a common floor.

For a viewer plotting the transition, the exercise is a gap analysis: place your background on the map, then use the season's episodes to cover the layers you have never owned. A developer's gap is usually infrastructure and operations; an ops person's gap is usually application architecture. The season that follows effectively walks both.
takeaway: Certification builds the shared three-layer base; your background determines which gaps the rest of the season must close for you.
